provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: PLACEMENT, not wording: the 1862 appoints this formulary to the SECOND SUNDAY AFTER EPIPHANY (its own date-line at line 54878, and it prints the commemoration of that Sunday, 'Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui coelestia simul et terrena moderaris', at lines 54911-54919). The 1962 appoints it to the Sunday falling 2-5 January, or failing that 2 January. Innocent XIII gave the feast the former place in 1721; Pius X moved it to the latter in 1913. The day moved; the prayer did not.; 1862 capitalises 'Unigenitum'; 1962 sets it lower case, 'unigenitum'.; 1862 prints 'coelis' with oe; 1962 prints 'caelis' with ae.; Conclusion: 1862 'Per eumdem Dominum nostrum.'; 1962 'Per eundem Dominum.' -- both the eumdem/eundem spelling and the length differ.; No difference of any other word, and none of the medial pointing: both set the colon after 'jussisti', the semicolon after 'propitius', and the comma after 'ut'.. Corroboration: None available and none claimed. The Venice 1570 and the Vatican typica 1604 both predate the feast's extension to the universal calendar by Innocent XIII in 1721, so their silence is expected and is evidence of nothing. I did run the search for the record -- 'clementissime', 'praedestinat', 'vocari iussisti' return nothing relevant in either book -- but a raw search over a degraded-latin OCR cannot found a negative and I do not offer it as one..

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui unigenitum Filium tuum constituisti humani generis Salvatorem, et
Jesum vocari jussisti: concede propitius; ut, cujus sanctum nomen veneramur
in terris, ejus quoque aspectu perfruamur in caelis. Per eundem Dominum.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 1861 keeps this feast on the Second Sunday after Epiphany, not on the Sunday between 2 and 5 January as the 1962 does. Leaf n104, printed p. 94, heads it `II. SUNDAY after EPIPHANY. The FEAST of the HOLY NAME JESUS.` over the Introit `In nomine Jesu`, and its Kalendar at leaf n774, printed p. 766, prints `Second Sunday after Epiphany- Feast of the most Holy Name of Jesus, d. of II. class 94`. The formulary is the same one, and the Latin cue set before this English is `Deus qui`, which answers the 1962's `Deus, qui Unigenitum`. The day placement is a recension difference and not a difference of text. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

translations.text: O God, who didst appoint thy only begotten Son the Saviour of mankind, and commandest that his name should be called JESUS: mercifully grant, that we who venerate his holy name on earth, may also enjoy his sight in heaven. Thro'.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Benedictio tua, clementissime Deus, qua omnis viget creatura, sanctificet,
quaesumus, hoc sacrificium nostrum, quod ad gloriam nominis Filii tui,
Domini nostri Jesu Christi, offerimus tibi: ut majestati tuae placere possit
ad laudem, et nobis proficere ad salutem. Per eundem Dominum nostrum Jesum
Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. Leaf n106, printed p. 96, running head `THE FEAST OF, &c.` The page sets no Latin cue before this Secret, and sets a second `SECRET of the Sunday` after it; the one recorded here is the first, the Mass's own. The conclusion is printed `Thro' the same.` Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

translations.text: May thy blessing, O most merciful God, by which every creature is enlivened and subsists, sanctify this our sacrifice, which we offer thee in honour of the name of thy Son, our Lord Jesus Christ: that it may be acceptable to the praise of thy majesty, and available to our salvation. Thro' the same.

provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 22-27; antecedent printed p. 379; text-layer lines 55056-55072 (heading 'Postcommunio.' at 55056, text 55058-55072)
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: PLACEMENT, as for the other two orations of this Mass.; 1862 sets a comma after 'creasti' ('qui creasti, et redemisti nos'); 1962 sets none.; 1862 sets no comma after 'Filii tui'; 1962 sets one.; 1862 prints 'coelis' with oe; 1962 prints 'caelis' with ae.; Conclusion: 1862 'Per eumdem Dominum nostrum.'; 1962 'Per eundem Dominum.'; Orthography: 1862 'majestati' with j; 1962 'maiestati' with i.; No difference of any word that the 1862 text layer renders legibly -- but see the notes: one word, 'suscipere', it does not render legibly at all.. Corroboration: None available and none claimed; the 1570 and 1604 predate the 1721 extension. The string 'praedestinationis' does occur in the 1604 at line 15772, but in a different prayer ('beatae praedestinationis liber') and it corroborates nothing here.. Recorded limitation: THIS IS THE WEAKEST ENTRY IN THE LANE AND THE ONE TO RE-CHECK FIRST. The 1862 text layer is visibly degraded across exactly this oration, and three of its marks are reconstructions rather than readings: line 55058 reads 'OMnfpotens setorne Deus?' where I have set 'Omnipotens aeterne Deus,' -- the '?' is almost certainly a comma, but I am inferring it from the 1962 and cannot see it; line 55064 reads 'Jesu Christi. majest&ti' with a full stop before a lower-case word, where I have set a comma; and line 55066 reads 'vultu susrinere digneris' where every other witness reads 'suscipere'. 'Susrinere' is not a Latin word and I have treated it as recogniser damage, which is what the artifact record leads one to expect of this scan, but I want it on the record that I did not READ 'suscipere' in the 1862 -- I inferred it. Also damaged and reconstructed the same way: 'redenristi' (55059) for 'redemisti', 'auod' (55062) for 'quod', 'titulogauded-mus' (55069) for 'titulo gaudeamus'. Those three are unambiguous; 'susrinere' is the one I would want a human to confirm. If leaf = printed page + 85 still holds here, the leaf to open is n464 for printed p. 379. I could not open it: the 1862 page images are remote and the brief forbids downloading. I am NOT rounding this up. The verdict is 'matched' because the prayer is unmistakably the same prayer and every legible word agrees; the confidence is 'medium' because one word of it is not legible in the only 1862 witness I was permitted to use. As printed, the 1962 reads 'Iesu Christi', 'maiestati' and 'nomine Iesu' with i.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Omnipotens aeterne Deus, qui creasti et redemisti nos, respice propitius
vota nostra: et sacrificium salutaris hostiae, quod in honorem nominis Filii
tui, Domini nostri Jesu Christi, majestati tuae obtulimus, placido et
benigno vultu suscipere digneris; ut gratia tua nobis infusa, sub glorioso
nomine Jesu, aeternae praedestinationis titulo gaudeamus nomina nostra
scripta esse in caelis. Per eundem Dominum.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Latin cue `Omnipotens`, answering the 1962's `Omnipotens aeterne Deus`. The page spells `honor` here and `honour` in the Secret above it; both are left as printed. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

translations.text: O almighty and eternal God, who didst both create and redeem us, mercifully hear our prayers, and vouchsafe, with a pleasing and kind countenance, to receive the sacrifice of this victim of our salvation, which we have offered to thy divine majesty, in honor of the name of thy Son, our Lord Jesus Christ; that thy grace being poured on us, thro' the glorious name of Jesus, as a pledge of our eternal predestination, we may rejoice that our names are written in heaven. Thro' the same.
